record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: Which words w can be obtained in more than one way from a single word u using different conducting sequences?

evidence.quote: Which words w can be obtained in more than one way from a single word u using different conducting sequences?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the setting of finite words over a finite alphabet, where one defines a fixed rewriting procedure that derives a new word from a given source word by applying a sequence of admissible elementary steps. Such a sequence of admissible steps applied to a source word $u$ is called a conducting sequence, and its output is the resulting word $w$.

Characterize all finite words $w$ with the following property: there exists a single source word $u$ and two distinct conducting sequences $S_1 \neq S_2$, both starting from $u$, such that applying $S_1$ to $u$ produces $w$ and applying $S_2$ to $u$ also produces $w$.

In other words, describe (structurally and/or combinatorially) the set of words $w$ that admit at least two different conducting sequences from one and the same word $u$.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface any subsequent paper resolving this question or providing a characterization of the words obtainable in more than one way from a single source word via different conducting sequences. The question appears in a compilation of open problems from the WORDS conferences (1997–2017); no later work specifically labelling this question as solved was located, so its current status could not be confirmed.
